question.worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=3{e}^{4t},$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}({e}^{2t})=2{e}^{2t}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(3{e}^{4t})}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =\frac{12{e}^{4t}}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =6{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=1,$ and we get

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,{|}_{t\,=\,1}=6{e}^{2(1)}=6{e}^{2}.
$$
